![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14134102/assets/50dfc42742418eae8eb25f26fd193b714e06b820f99945ac2b8b759eed3a349e.png)

Consider the figure shown above. Which of the following triplets of points are collinear?

I. $Q,S,T$

II. $M,O,Q$

III. $N,P,T$
question.worked_solution:
- $Q,S,T$ are collinear since there is a straight line that passes through all of them.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14134102/assets/2101dd8ae066aa55d601263de389e013100e476ddbf5220381e4040440b344a9.png)

- $M,O,Q$ are **not** collinear since we can't draw a straight line that passes through all of them.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14134102/assets/d29ca68ff7123964944eded292ec8ea2c6b16a9fd46e875472e7666f114c8cad.png)

- $N,P,T$ are **not** collinear since we can't draw a straight line that passes through all of them.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14134102/assets/03db0865e93c7c9a1a2f1c23fd8027602e04299903edb6996b9f0b2150d1d036.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
